-117.26200,34.04720.name: Loma Linda University Center for Fertility and IVF
-117.26200,34.04720.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Gihan M. Bareh, MD, PHD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-80.19360,25.77416.name: Miami Veterans Affairs Healthcare System
-80.19360,25.77416.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Veterans Affairs. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.64215,53.33205.name: Care Fertility Cheshire
-2.64215,53.33205.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-75.69500,45.38586.name: Carleton University
-75.69500,45.38586.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, October 2025
-75.69500,45.38586.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, October 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

149.13000,-35.28090.name: Office of the Gene Technology Regulator — GMO Record
149.13000,-35.28090.desc: Australia’s regulator, and one of the few that publishes where field trials actually are — EU member states do too, under the deliberate release directive, in several countries down to the parcel. Every other release record on this map sits at a state or country centroid because the register gives no location; Australia gives coordinates, licence conditions and risk assessments. It shows that publishing sites is possible and that everyone else has chosen not to.

-96.80200,32.78800.name: Colossal Foundation
-96.80200,32.78800.desc: The de-extinction company's non-profit arm, funding conservation work on living endangered species alongside the extinct ones. The structure is worth recording: a venture-funded company raising money on mammoths while a foundation attached to it does conventional conservation, so the publicity from one supports the other.

103.84000,1.27000.name: Wilmar International
103.84000,1.27000.desc: The largest palm oil processor in the world. Palm is the highest-yielding oil crop by far and the one most associated with deforestation, and engineered and edited palm is under development to raise yields further. Whether that reduces land pressure or increases the return on clearing more is the question, and it will be settled by companies at this end of the chain rather than by the breeders.
